page: Amazon Web Services c6g.medium is a compute-optimized instance powered by a custom AWS Graviton2 processor built on the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. It features 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 2.0 GB of DDR4 memory. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, does not include local storage, and has a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the c6g.medium demonstrates a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test yields a score of 1493.38, placing it in the average category. However, due to its single-core limitation, multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core fall into the lower performance tier. Memory bandwidth tests also register in the lower tier, with read-only small block cached memory at 59.29 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 9.83 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c6g.medium offers a low-cost entry point into the ARM64 ecosystem with dedicated CPU resources rather than shared-core burstable allocations. However, the lack of local storage, 0 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and low memory capacity limit its utility for resource-intensive applications. This instance is suited for lightweight single-threaded tasks, simple web serving, basic code compilation, and minor background processing workloads that do not require high memory bandwidth or multi-threaded execution.

It is equipped with 2.0 GB of memory, 32 MB of L3 cache, and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with no local storage. Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core CPU capabilities, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1493.38. However, its single-core design and low memory capacity result in lower-tier multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 933.0 and a large-block write speed of 9.83 GB/sec. Qualitatively, the c6g.medium provides a cost-efficient entry point for dedicated ARM64 compute resources. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic web serving, and simple background utility tasks.
